findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact GerritClient method voter.py will call to obtain the revision file map for anchor validation (add a general per-revision file-list getter if get_merge_files' merge-only scope and MAGIC_PATHS are unsuitable), and state whether MAGIC_PATHS are excluded from partition_findings' revision_paths.
evidence: Plan: 'best-effort fetch of the revision file map to validate anchors'
gerrit_client.py:184 get_merge_files docstring: 'the auto-merge-base file map for a MERGE revision'; a CLEAN merge 'yields only the magic /COMMIT_MSG + /MERGE_LIST pseudo-paths'
No general per-revision file-list getter exists in gerrit_client.py (only get_merge_files, get_file_diff, get_mergelist)
findings.finding: The plan's voter.py delta relies on a 'best-effort fetch of the revision file map' to populate partition_findings' revision_paths, but names no GerritClient method for it; the only existing map-returning method is get_merge_files, which is documented as MERGE-revision-specific and returns synthetic MAGIC_PATHS (/COMMIT_MSG, /MERGE_LIST) alongside real files.
scenarios: A non-merge change: no client method is named to obtain its file map
A merge revision: get_merge_files returns only the auto-merge delta plus MAGIC_PATHS, so anchors to files present in the full patchset but outside the conflict delta would be classified anchor-less

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete truncation defaults in the plan: max characters per rendered finding line and the max number of findings enumerated before the 'N additional omitted' note fires.
evidence: 'per-line truncation, and an explicit "N additional ... omitted" overflow note'
No numeric per-line length or enumeration cap appears anywhere in the plan or ACs
findings.finding: render_findings_block specifies 'per-line truncation' and an 'N additional ... omitted' overflow note but never states the actual limits (max chars per line, max findings enumerated before overflow). The executor must invent both values, and AC4 tests could pin arbitrary numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit defaults, e.g. 'truncate each finding line to 500 chars with an ellipsis; enumerate at most 50 findings, then append "N additional advisory finding(s) omitted — see REVIEW_RESULT sidecar"', and assert those bounds in an AC4 sub-case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify AC3: name the record precisely as the code_review artifact ticket's REVIEW_RESULT sidecar, and state the behaviour when that best-effort emission failed (so the notice does not reference a non-existent record).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:26 EVENT_TYPE = "REVIEW_RESULT"; sidecar.emit returns False 'on any failure (best-effort — never raises)'

src/rebar/review_bot/artifact_emit.py:56-168 emit_code_review_artifact creates/reuses a code_review artifact ticket and calls sidecar.emit; the whole path is best-effort and returns None on failure (ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR marker)
The REVIEW_RESULT sidecar lands on artifact_id (the code_review artifact ticket), not on the rebar work ticket the operator would inspect
findings.finding: AC3 names 'the ticket's REVIEW_RESULT sidecar as the full record', but the review-bot's REVIEW_RESULT sidecar is emitted (via emit_code_review_artifact -> code_review.sidecar.emit, EVENT_TYPE='REVIEW_RESULT') on a GENERATED code_review artifact ticket (title 'code-review: <change> @ <rev>'), not on the rebar work ticket, and emission is best-effort AND can itself fail (swallowed, returns None). The sidecar existence claim is confirmed by code, but the fallback notice's usefulness rests on that emission having succeeded — a dependency the plan does not state.
findings.location: AC3 / Plan 'voter.py' bullet ('appended notice naming the ticket's REVIEW_RESULT sidecar as the full record')
scenarios: A comment-bearing POST fails AND emit_code_review_artifact previously failed (write-dead store): the fallback notice points a reader at a REVIEW_RESULT sidecar that was never written
An operator reads the notice and looks for the sidecar on the rebar work ticket rather than the generated code_review artifact ticket

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extract the existing enumeration/truncation/overflow logic from adapter.py `_summarize` (the 'finding' branch, lines 142-151) into the shared `render_findings_block` and have both the blocking list and the new advisory block call it, rather than writing a second parallel formatter.
evidence: Plan: 'render_findings_block(findings, kind) — enumerated `- (criterion) detail [location]` lines, per-line truncation, and an explicit "N additional ... omitted" overflow note.'

adapter.py:142-151 already does exactly this: `for f in blocking[:10]` builds `- ({crit}) {detail}{loc}`, truncates at 240 chars with an ellipsis, and appends `{omitted} additional blocking {noun} omitted from this summary.`

Two independent implementations of the same line-format + truncation + overflow behavior invite drift (e.g. the existing cap is 10 and truncation is 240 chars; the new module does not state whether it matches).
findings.finding: render_findings_block re-implements the enumeration/truncation/overflow-note logic that adapter.py:141-152 already contains, rather than extracting and reusing it.
scenarios: A future change to the truncation length or overflow wording updates only one of the two formatters, so PASS/BLOCK body enumeration and the advisory block diverge in format.
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor _summarize's blocking loop to call render_findings_block(blocking, kind='blocking'), then reuse the same function for the advisory block, so cap (10), 240-char truncation, and overflow wording live in exactly one place.
